Update an Existing SEM Graph

Source: R/plot-update_graph.R
update_graph.Rd

update_graph() modifies an existing sem_graph object while preserving its manually specified geometry and aesthetics.

Unlike prepare_graph(), which constructs a graph from a layout, update_graph() operates on coordinates that have already been scaled and prepared for plotting.

Node bounding boxes are recalculated using the current node coordinates and dimensions. Individual node dimensions take precedence over the graph's global shape dimensions.

Usage

update_graph(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sem_graph'
update_graph(x, nodes = NULL, edges = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

An object of class sem_graph.

...

Additional graph-level plotting settings to update, such as rect_width, rect_height, ellipses_width, ellipses_height, variance_diameter, text_size, spacing_x, spacing_y, or fix_coord.

nodes

Optional data frame containing replacement node information. If NULL, the existing nodes are retained.

edges

Optional data frame containing replacement edge information. If NULL, the existing edges are retained.

Value

An updated object of class sem_graph.

Details

Modify the nodes, edges, or plotting settings of an existing structural equation model (SEM) graph without recalculating its layout or automatically repositioning its edges.

The function preserves existing node positions and does not apply layout spacing a second time.

Node bounding boxes (node_xmin, node_xmax, node_ymin, and node_ymax) are recalculated from node centers and dimensions.

If a node has individual width or height values, these override the corresponding global shape dimensions.

The following properties are preserved unless explicitly modified:

  • Node coordinates (x, y).

  • Edge connection sides (connect_from, connect_to).

  • Edge curvature.

  • Variance-loop positions.

  • Node and edge labels.

  • Node and edge aesthetics.

For self-variance edges with arrow = "both", the source and target connection sides are kept synchronized.

Changing spacing_x or spacing_y does not rescale existing node coordinates.

See also

prepare_graph(), update_graph_node()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Construct a graph
g <- prepare_graph(
  edges = edges,
  nodes = nodes,
  layout = layout
)

# Change node positions
nd <- g$nodes
nd$x[nd$name == "visual"] <- 5

g <- update_graph(g, nodes = nd)

# Change edge aesthetics
ed <- g$edges
ed$colour <- "black"
ed$colour[1] <- "steelblue"

g <- update_graph(g, edges = ed)

# Change global plotting settings
g <- update_graph(
  g,
  text_size = 5,
  variance_diameter = 1
)

plot(g)
} # }
